gemma4-rp-maxxed-q3kxl.why: Cleanest output on every check: 100% of raw lines pass all checks, no refusal or moralising on the grim set, intent 97% (the only model above 80%), no repetition loops, best conversation turn-taking, 100% right tool in both tool_choice modes, and the reflection JSON always parses. It is the slowest of the four (about 137 tok/s decode, 0.31 s cold first token, 0.08 s warm) but a 12-17 token line is still back in under 0.25 s warm even with three slots busy.
caveats: Its 6% sanitizer drop rate is not the model's fault: all 6 drops are the agent sanitizer rejecting sentence-initial 'It' (see Findings, F1). It also loses 5% of reflection runs to a possessive ('Hana's') the same sanitizer rejects (F2).
Tool arguments ignore the numeric ranges 20% of the time (importance 100, delta -20); clamp them in the tool executor (F4).
12.7 GB of VRAM with the shape the engine chose (3 x 65536, q4_0 KV); the size worker owns whether that leaves the game its room.

ling3-tiny-q4km.why: Fastest model by a wide margin (about 310 tok/s decode, 0.035 s warm first token) and the best tool-call behaviour (100% of arguments validate, round-2 works). The `--jinja` template is not a problem: no thinking leaks, no template residue, tool calls parse. Its weakness is language use, not plumbing.
caveats: Intent labelling is poor: 43% against 30 labelled lines (kind read as comfort, insult as slight). Do not trust the intent label from Ling; either give the intent pass a stronger model or accept noisy relationship effects.

4% of raw lines are not in first-person speech: third-person narration ('Tuk feels the bandage. Tuk does not like it.', 'Tuk is crouched, bow drawn...') and '- ' bullets. The sanitizer does not catch either (F3).
Low diversity: 17 of 100 lines are exact duplicates ("I think, well, probably it's fine." eight times) and 2 of 10 conversations loop.
Over-eager tool use: it calls say() on prompts that say no action is needed (40% of no-tool prompts).

gemma4-e4b-q4km.why: 100% of raw lines pass every check, no refusals, no loops, no cross-speaker writing, intent 80%, and about 130 tok/s. A sound mid-size choice, held back by tool-call plumbing and weaker reflection acceptance.
caveats: Gemma-format tool calls leak into content on 2 of 30 auto-mode prompts (the text `remember{fact:<|"|>...<|"|>,importance:2}`), so llama-server's parser missed them.
Tool arguments out of range 16% of the time (importance 10, delta -10).

After a tool result it answers with an empty reply in 64% of round-two turns (HTTP fine, `finish_reason: stop`, no content). That is acceptable for a game that treats the call as the action, but a loop that waits for text will stall.
Only 85% of reflections are accepted (possessive 'Hana's', F2); two-call prompts 80% right.

gemma4-e2b-q4km.why: Plausible lines (99% raw pass, 0 refusals) at 190 tok/s with 3 GB of VRAM, so it is the fallback for small cards. Everything beyond a single line is weak.
caveats: Conversations repeat: 4 of 10 exchanges loop, typically a speaker repeating its own earlier line verbatim; 5 duplicate lines of 100 singles.
Intent 60% with the agent's grammar; json_schema enum mode is unusable (30% valid) though the agent does not use it.
Tool use is the least reliable: 80% right tool in auto mode, 5 of 30 tool calls left as raw Gemma syntax in content, 68% of arguments in range, and round two returns an empty reply 100% of the time.
85% of reflections accepted; some bios start with 'Quiet is easier now.' and trip the name check.
